n88df928e4c65: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.
n9a95df70102a: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.
n655877e57217: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.
nfd78a74cc8d9: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.
n789e4ad2e301: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.
nbe59f49b00ea: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.
n0147da51a5b2: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.
n01db1bbde499: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.
n0c668217e858: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.
n6bce9b30997a: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.
n2e3bfb7ddc8f: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental–computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load–displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

n7bb1231a501d: Background This study translated, culturally adapted, and evaluated the First Aid Willingness Questionnaire for Schoolchildren to assess adolescents’ self-reported readiness to help and potential barriers to first-aid provision. Methods This cross-sectional psychometric study included 470 high school students in Aksaray, Türkiye. The questionnaire underwent forward–backward translation, review by 12 experts, and pilot testing with 35 students. Exploratory factor analysis derived the structure, which was subsequently evaluated via ordinal confirmatory factor analysis in the same sample. Content and construct validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance across gender, grade level, and perceived family income were assessed. Results All item-level content validity ratios exceeded 0.83; the scale-level content validity index was 0.90. Removing two items yielded a 16-item, three-factor structure: First Aid Willingness, Negative Emotions, and Perceived Knowledge. The model showed acceptable fit: scaled χ²(101) = 288.09, p < 0.001; comparative fit index = 0.95; Tucker–Lewis index = 0.94; root mean square error of approximation = 0.06, 90% confidence interval [0.05, 0.07]; standardized root mean square residual = 0.06. Composite reliability ranged from 0.79 to 0.90. Average variance extracted ranged from 0.49 to 0.59, with borderline convergent validity for Negative Emotions. Discriminant validity was supported. Cronbach’s alpha ranged from 0.72 to 0.87, and McDonald’s omega from 0.74 to 0.87. Configural, threshold, metric, and scalar invariance were supported across all grouping variables. Strict invariance was supported across grade level and perceived family income, but not gender. Conclusion The results provide preliminary evidence for the Turkish questionnaire’s psychometric properties and support subscale interpretation and latent mean comparisons within the study sample. Independent replication and evaluation of temporal stability, responsiveness, and external validity are needed.
n1b74a46a6268: Due to their low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity, accurately classifying EEG signals is still one of the main hindrances that limit the real-world applications of a brain-computer interface (BCI). Deep learning (DL) is a potential method for addressing the problem. However, how to create a suitable DL network for motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs poses severe challenges in the case of insufficient training data. In this paper, a DL network based on multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal and channel attention mechanisms is proposed for decoding MI tasks. Temporal and spatial features are extracted by four parallel CNN branches, each of which is followed by a Transformer block for learning the global correlations of local time features. The outputs from the four Transformer blocks are concatenated along channel dimension and then input into a channel attention module for channel fusion. The subsequent feature map is classified by a CNN, which replaces the commonly used fully connected layer for reducing computational complexity. The proposed network was evaluated on three publicly available BCI datasets and compared with five state-of-the-art DL networks. The training data sets are augmented using the approach segmentation and reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 80.21% on Dataset 1 (4-class tasks), 90.19% on Dataset 2 (2-class tasks), and 97.32% on Dataset 3 (4-class tasks), surpassing the strongest baselines FBCNet on Dataset 1, MSFBCNN on Dataset 2 and MSFBCNN on Dataset 3 by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99% respectively. The network effectively decoded the MI-based EEG signals, providing a potential method for BCI applications.
n8036ff01abf1: Leaf day respiratory rate (Rd), a pivotal component of plant carbon metabolism that directly modulates net photosynthetic carbon gain and plant fitness, has long been challenging to accurately quantify due to overlapping CO2 fluxes with photosynthesis and photorespiration (Rp). This study aimed to disentangle Rd from Rp in C3 crops using a high-CO2/low-O2 (>1200 μmol mol–1 CO2 + 2% O2) An/Ca (net photosynthetic rate-ambient CO2 concentration) model. We integrated two datasets: An/Ca curve data of four C3 species (Trifolium pratense, Silphium perfoliatum, Lolium perenne, Triticum aestivum) under ambient O2 (21% O2) from Ye et al. (2025) and newly collected data under low O2 (2% O2) for the same species. A dedicated model (Eqn 1) was developed to extract key parameters [e.g., the maximum net photosynthetic rate (Anmax), CO2 compensation point (Γ) in the presence of Rd, photorespiratory rate at Ca = 0 μmol mol–1 (RC0)] from An/Ca curves, with ANOVA confirming no significant differences between calculated and observed parameter values (p > 0.05). Under 2% O2, Rp was strongly suppressed, making the gross photorespiratory rate (RC = Rp + Rd) a reliable proxy for approximate Rd. Results showed that Rd estimates from the high-CO2/low-O2 approach (0.74–1.12 μmol m–2 s–1) were consistent with literature ranges (0.74–2.89 μmol m–2 s–1) for four C3 crops. Interspecific differences in Rd were observed: L. perenne had the highest Rd, while T. aestivum had the lowest, which correlated with species-specific photosynthetic traits (e.g., carboxylation efficiency). Rd remained stable across O2 levels (21% vs. 2%), indicating independence from short-term photorespiratory flux changes. The RC ≈ Rd assumption is supported by the substantial decrease in Γ (50–67%) and RCO (40–55%) under 2% O2, and by the consistency of Rd estimates with literature ranges, although independent ground-truth measurements remain to be conducted. This study suggests the high-CO2/low-O2 An/Ca model as a new tool for Rd quantification in C3 crops. The findings enhance understanding of non-photosynthetic carbon flux dynamics and provide critical parameters for refining crop carbon cycling models to predict growth and yield under current and future atmospheric conditions.
n573f4e19954d: Background Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors. Methods A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology – considered the “gold standard” – was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21–24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer. Results Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff. Conclusion The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.
ndfe4e55cb195: Banana breeding programs prioritize improving yield with resistance to biotic stresses while maintaining fruit quality. This study focused on identifying genotypes with resistance to five major biotic constraints including Cosmopolites sordidus, Radopholus similis, banana Xanthomonas wilt, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense – Race 1 and Pseudocercospora fijiensis. A diverse set of diploid and tetraploid genotypes was phenotyped under controlled screenhouse and field conditions to identify potential sources of. A partially replicated (P-rep) design, was used to accommodate unequal plant availability arising from asynchronous multiplication. P-rep design enabled robust phenotypic comparisons and identification of genotypes expressing resistance to multiple biotic stresses. Several diploid genotypes exhibited resistance to multiple constraints, highlighting their potential as parental lines for resistance introgression and broadening the genetic base for banana improvement. Leveraging on the efficiency and precision of the P-rep experimental design, these findings accelerate the phenotyping of genotypes.
n730a07c03273: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users’ medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people’s intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users’ data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users’ perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users’ intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = −0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users’ intentions to adopt mHealth apps.
n849824774335: Participation equity is essential for ensuring that students gain cognitive and social benefits from collaborative learning, yet there is a lack of quantitative benchmarks for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in small-group collaboration. This study focuses on two turn-based analytical dimensions of participation equity: participation equality, measured by students’ shares of speaking turns, and opportunity equality, measured by students’ shares of addressed opportunities. Using the standard deviation of these rates, the study establishes preliminary, context-specific simulation-based reference values for identifying departures from an idealized triadic turn-taking baseline. The empirical dataset included 117 fourth-grade primary school students from two classes in mainland China, who worked in heterogeneous triads on mathematical and reading tasks. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulation, the study estimated local turn-taking parameters from empirical data, generated reference distributions under an ideal-equity baseline, and conducted sensitivity analyses to examine model stability. Results support the internal stability of the model and provide turn-count-specific reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity inequality. The findings offer preliminary reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in collaborative learning and highlight the importance of turn count when evaluating structural patterns of participation and opportunity in triadic classroom dialogue. These reference values describe structural participation patterns rather than collaboration quality and require recalibration and independent validation before application in other educational settings.
n449fbe7b610b: by Md. Aftabur Rahman, Lamyea Kabir, Nadia Ahmed, Atish Barua, Mohammad Hasan, Ahmad Abdullah Mahdeen Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.
n4ab5d48faeff: Preclinical thoracic micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is constrained by the brief pulmonary enhancement window of intravenously (IV) administered iodinated contrast, which the kidneys clear rapidly. We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. IV delivery produced vascular and cardiac opacification with progressive bladder accumulation, which was the largest signal in every IV animal by 120 min. Intratracheal delivery produced widespread, comparatively uniform lung-parenchymal opacification at 5, 15 and 30 min with no discrete bladder opacity at any time; coronal thoracic signal was 0.77 at 5 min and 0.72 at 30 min, against 0.09 to 0.19 after IV injection. Acute safety was assessed at 5 and 29 h by serum biochemistry and histopathology against untreated controls. ALT, AST and blood urea nitrogen did not differ among groups. Creatinine was modestly higher than in controls after both routes, with no difference between routes, consistent with renal excretion of absorbed iohexol. Lung, heart, liver, spleen and kidney showed preserved architecture without acute injury. These data identify intratracheal microspray delivery as a practical way to hold iodine in the lung parenchyma across a thoracic micro-CT acquisition and provide the basis for a confirmatory quantitative study.
n25e6e52d2d5e: Purpose Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) is a recognized anterior-segment manifestation of fibrillinopathy. This exploratory phenotype-first study compared macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters between participants with and without documented lens dislocation and descriptively reviewed available archived clinical FBN1 reports. Methods This retrospective, availability-based study included 16 participants classified by verified current or historical lens-dislocation status. Participant-level superficial capillary plexus (SCP) vessel density was calculated by averaging valid bilateral measurements or using the single valid eye. Five OCTA endpoints were compared using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests; Benjamini–Hochberg q values were used as a multiplicity sensitivity analysis. Seven archived clinical FBN1 reports from lens-dislocation-positive (LD+) participants were summarized without variant reclassification. No genotype–OCTA association was assessed. Results The cohort comprised 7 LD+ and 9 lens-dislocation-negative (LD−) participants; 15 participants (6 LD+ and 9 LD−) contributed quantitative OCTA data. Foveal SCP vessel density was lower in LD+ participants (median [IQR], 19.38% [18.68–20.04] vs 30.20% [29.20–31.85]; p = 0.036), but the finding was not retained after multiplicity sensitivity analysis (q = 0.180). Whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal vessel-density comparisons were not significant (p = 0.328, 0.272, and 0.238; q = 0.410 each), and OD-only foveal avascular zone area did not differ (n = 14; p = 0.606; q = 0.606). Six of seven archived reports documented an FBN1 variant; one was negative within its assay scope. Conclusions The unadjusted foveal signal was not robust to multiplicity analysis, and other OCTA endpoints did not differ significantly. Marked between-group differences in spherical equivalent and axial length, the small sample, and heterogeneous routine-care genetic reports limit interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish OCTA as a diagnostic or prognostic test or demonstrate an individual-level genotype–OCTA association.
na4b04818df1b: Thermally delayed biomass-boiler systems exhibit heterogeneous temporal responses that complicate forecasting and operational warning. This study analysed long-term field data from a biomass-fired boiler system to characterise thermal-response lags and evaluate multi-horizon forecasting of the P1 thermal-storage-tank temperature at 60-, 120-, and 180-min horizons. Robust cross-correlation analysis showed statistically detectable but weak associations between P1 temperature and the combustion-related operational inputs, while daily lag estimates exhibited broad and heterogeneous distributions, indicating that the system could not be represented by a single deterministic response time. Benchmark comparison showed that increasing model complexity did not necessarily improve forecasting performance. The Linear AR model achieved the lowest test RMSE and highest R2 at all three horizons, with RMSE values of 1.3774, 2.1605, and 2.6182 °C and R2 values of 0.7809, 0.4616, and 0.2104 at 60, 120, and 180 min, respectively. Lag coverage increased with forecasting horizon, whereas predictive accuracy progressively decreased, demonstrating a trade-off between pointwise accuracy and coverage of delayed thermal responses rather than a universally optimal horizon. Retrospective out-of-band warning analysis further showed that XGBoost recall decreased from 0.5343 at 60 min to 0.1761 at 120 min and 0.0538 at 180 min, while specificity increased from 0.9095 to 0.9546 and 0.9854, respectively. These results indicate that longer-horizon forecasts became increasingly conservative and detected progressively fewer future out-of-band states. Overall, the findings demonstrate that simple temporal models remain highly competitive for this strongly persistent thermal system and that multi-horizon forecasts should be interpreted as predictive risk indicators rather than evidence of causal improvements in boiler control or operational performance.
n06ad09260b2a: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble bioactive compound with significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, is widely utilized in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. In this study, we established a multi-enzyme cascade system in engineered Escherichia coli to synthesize DSS from L-Tyrosine. The initial co-expression of 4-hydroxyphenylacetate 3-monooxygenase (HpaBC), L-amino acid deaminase (aadL), glucose dehydrogenase (gdh) and D-lactate dehydrogenase (ldhD) yielded 5.1 mM DSS. The production of DSS increased to 6.53 mM through optimizing plasmid copy number. After optimizing the conditions, the yield of DSS reached 8.66 mM from strain 6. Finally, whole cell biotransformation using strain 6 in bioreactor yielded 19.47 mM DSS within 32h. These findings provide valuable insights for the scalable biosynthesis of pharmaceutically important compound of DSS from naturally available substrates of L-Tyrosine.
ne33e0253ccc9: The TTC22 gene encodes a protein containing seven tetratricopeptide repeats (TPRs), which mediate protein‒protein interactions as chaperones. We previously reported that the level of TTC22 transcript variant 1 (TTC22v1) was downregulated in human colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and that TTC22 upregulated m6A-mediated WTAP and SNAI1 expression via the TTC22‒RPL4 interaction and subsequently promoted COAD metastasis. Thus, a commercially available C57BL/6N mouse model in which the Ttc22 exon 2&3 encoding the TPR4 (equal to the human TTC22 TPR3) domain was knocked out via CRISPR-Cas9 was used to evaluate the contribution of Ttc22 to the development of mice and COAD. To determine the status of Ttc22 expression in Ttc22 knockout mice, we prepared a rabbit polyclonal antibody against the mouse Ttc22 protein, which could bind both wild-type Ttc22 and TPR4-deleted Ttc22 proteins overexpressed in HEK293T cells, as determined by Western blot analysis. Ttc22 proteins were detected in colon tissue samples from wild-type mice and Ttc22 hemi-knockout (Ttc22+/-) mice but not in those from fully Ttc22 knockout (Ttc22-/-) mice. Unfortunately, the long-term observation results demonstrated that Ttc22 knockout (KO, including Ttc22+/- or Ttc22-/-) did not affect the body weight, development, fertility, or spontaneous tumor incidence of male or female mice. No differences in the incidence of AOM/DSS-induced COAD were observed between these mouse groups, although Ttc22 deletion partially resulted in the upregulation of genes related to the host adaptive response to inflammation in the colon mucosa. In conclusion, no phenotypes were induced by Ttc22 inactivation in C57BL/6N mice.
n1136c6b6284f: High pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) poses a serious threat to captive rare birds. Because effective countermeasures are limited, the use of human antiviral drugs to treat HPAIV infections in captive rare birds has been considered. Although the human antiviral drug, baloxavir marboxil (BXM), is not approved for the treatment of influenza virus infection in birds, previous studies demonstrated the antiviral efficacy of BXM in experimental avian models. Pharmacokinetic studies have also revealed substantial interspecies differences following BXM administration, suggesting the need to establish species-specific dosing regimens. In this study, BXM was administered to 14 avian species to optimize dosing regimens for each species. Oral administration of BXM using different methods revealed that drug–food interactions had a limited impact on systemic drug exposure. Pharmacokinetic analysis of BXM and its active metabolite, baloxavir acid (BXA), demonstrated marked interspecies variability in drug exposure, contributing to the development of optimized dosing regimens for each species. Furthermore, systemic exposure to BXA was strongly associated with drug absorption indicators, suggesting that species-specific differences in absorption efficiency largely determine BXA exposure among avian species. This study provides a pharmacokinetic basis for the rational use of BXM in diverse avian species. It contributes to the development of practical antiviral strategies to protect captive rare birds against HPAIVs.
n123427a6d7bd: Background Women living with HIV (WLHIV) face a sixfold increased risk of cervical cancer compared to HIV-negative women. Most WLHIV residing in the Southern and Eastern African regions have a substantial HIV-related cervical cancer burden. Studies on precancerous cervical lesions (PCCL) and associated factors in WLHIV from these regions have inconsistent and inconclusive findings. Therefore, we aimed to synthesize the pooled prevalence of PCCL and associated factors among WLHIV in Southern and Eastern Africa. Methods This study was registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251123583) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 standards. Primary studies published from inception to 2025 in Southern and Eastern Africa were included. The methodological quality of studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Data extraction and statistical analyses were done in Microsoft Excel and STATA 17, respectively. Pooled prevalence, publication bias, subgroup, and sensitivity analysis were conducted. Associations were expressed as odds ratios (OR), and a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results 44 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a sample size of 47,009. The pooled prevalence of PCCL was 22.25% (95% CI: 19.57, 24.93). Age at first sexual intercourse (< 18 years) (OR = 2.99, (2.34, 3.82)), multiparity (OR = 4.97, (3.21, 7.69)), having multiple sexual partners (OR = 3.06 (2.45, 3.83)), having a history of sexually transmitted infections (STI) (OR = 3.93 (3.23, 4.78)), smoking (OR = 7.01, (3.39, 14.49)), ever taking oral contraceptive pills (OR = 2.69, (1.85, 3.90)), low CD4 count (OR = 1.79, (1.56, 2.05)), and having not initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) (OR = 2.02, (1.56, 2.62)) were significantly associated with an increased risk of PCCL. Conclusion and recommendations The pooled prevalence of PCCL was high. Additionally, early first sexual intercourse, parity, STIs, multiple sexual partners, smoking, oral contraceptive use, CD4 count, and ART were positively associated with the occurrence of PCCL. Therefore, stakeholders shall implement interventions to avert future incidents of PCCL and address the identified factors.
n8b166a4ae64e: Phonation-induced acoustic variability, particularly in whispered speech, poses persistent challenges for stable vowel representation. Conventional static formant-based descriptors often fail to capture the dynamic spectral behavior of vowels under such conditions. This study evaluates the robustness of acoustic feature representations for Japanese vowels across normal and whispered phonation, comparing static formant measures with dynamic spectral features derived from Vowel Inherent Spectral Change (VISC). Dynamic features are used to characterize continuous formant trajectory patterns, while Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) classifiers serve as analytical probes to assess representation stability rather than as targets of algorithmic optimization. Results demonstrate that incorporating dynamic spectral information leads to more consistent vowel discrimination across phonation types compared to static-only representations, with similar performance trends observed across classification frameworks. These findings suggest that differences in classification outcomes are primarily driven by properties of the acoustic representations rather than by model choice. The study highlights the im-portance of representation-level design for robust speech signal analysis under phonation-induced variability and supports the use of low-dimensional dynamic features for vowel modeling in variable phonation conditions.
n9fc5c5b3632b: Background Professional identity is fundamental to nursing education and influences students’ academic development, clinical practice, and career commitment. This study examined the associations of empathy and Big Five personality traits with professional identity among Chinese undergraduate nursing students. Methods A cross-sectional observational study was conducted among undergraduate nursing students in Chongqing, China. Participants completed the Interpersonal Reactivity Index–Chinese version (IRI-C), Ten-Item Personality Inventory–Chinese version (TIPI-C), and Professional Identity Questionnaire for Medical Students (PIQMS). Data were analysed using Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression analyses. Results A total of 274 nursing undergraduates were included. Professional identity was positively correlated with overall empathy (r = 0.196, P r = 0.407, P β = 0.231), perspective taking (β = 0.219), conscientiousness (β = 0.204), personal distress (β = 0.154), extraversion (β = 0.132), and neuroticism (β = 0.131) were independently associated with higher professional identity. The model explained 28% of the variance in professional identity (adjusted R² = 0.28). Conclusion Professional identity among nursing undergraduates was associated with empathy, personality traits, and perceptions of nurse–patient relationships. These findings support the integration of empathy-focused training and personality-informed educational strategies into undergraduate nursing education to strengthen professional identity.
n33525d22f335: Pulsed electric field ablation is an emerging non-thermal modality for tumor treatment, in which electroporation of both the plasma membrane and the nuclear envelope plays a critical role in inducing irreversible cellular damage. To elucidate the different effects of nanosecond pulsed electric fields (nsPEFs) on these membranes, we compared the electroporation responses of the single and double membranes under the same field strength employing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Our results demonstrate that the double membrane underwent faster electroporation, attributed to inter-membrane counter-deformation under Coulomb force, which modulated the local electric field direction and reduced membrane tension. Compared to the single membrane, the double membrane may be more susceptible to damage induced by nsPEFs. This finding may provide a molecular-scale theoretical reference for understanding the electroporation mechanism of the nuclear envelope relative to the plasma membrane under nsPEFs.
naf21ffe879a4: Liver transplantation (LT) is a complex surgical intervention, with intricate decision-making and risks at all stages before, during and after the procedure itself. Artificial intelligence (AI) may assist the process but has seen limited use. This scoping review assessed primary articles reporting on clinical AI in LT in MEDLINE and Embase from 2000 to September 2026. 196 articles were identified: focusing on the pre-operative period before transplant (21.9%), organ retrieval (9.7%), intra-operative issues (3.6%), short-term post-operative complications (16.8%), long-term post-operative complications (45.9%) and natural language processing (2.0%). 95.9% had retrospective designs and only 12.8% had direct multi-centre data, with the rest from national registries or single centres. 13.8% of studies externally validated their AI tools. Only one study performed a prospective evaluation of their tool with a randomized controlled trial. Progress towards clinically deployable tools will require harmonised, higher-granularity datasets, consistent reporting, and prospective evaluation within real-world transplant workflows.
n362862988178: Generating high ball speed is crucial for achieving competitive baseball pitching performance. The lower extremity mechanics play a key role in generating high ball speed during a baseball pitch. However, some previous studies have reported no significant difference in ball speeds despite differences in lower extremity mechanics, highlighting the need to examine how energy is transferred through the upper extremity to the ball under these conditions. This study examined how upper extremity energy flow differed across stride-length conditions in relation to the observed differences in ball speed. Twenty college baseball pitchers pitched with under-stride length (US) and over-stride length (OS) in addition to normal-stride length (NS). We analyzed the mechanical energy of the upper extremity segments at key events during pitching, and the energy flow through each joint between events. The mechanical energy in the proximal segments at the stride foot contact increased as the stride length extended. In contrast, the mechanical energy in the distal segments at maximum external rotation in the shoulder joint was greater in the NS than in the US and OS, consistent with ball speed differences. During this phase, the energy flow to the upper arm through the shoulder joint was greater in the NS than in the US and OS, and the same condition pattern was observed for energy transfer through the elbow and wrist joints and for ball speed. Additionally, although no statistically significant difference in ball speed was observed between the US and OS, the JFP and STP components of shoulder energy flow showed different condition patterns, suggesting that shoulder energy flow composition may differ even when no statistically significant difference is observed in total energy flow into the upper arm.
n64b89f0b6110: Passive disease surveillance systems may systematically undercount burden in low-resource minority neighborhoods, yet fine-scale evidence of this phenomenon remains limited. We examined spatiotemporal patterns of reported COVID-19 cases across Miami-Dade County's diverse neighborhoods and investigated which socioeconomic and demographic characteristics predicted areas of elevated and suppressed case rates. In an ecological, cross-sectional analysis of 491,769 geocoded cases across 1,831 census block groups from March 2020 to May 2021, we applied negative binomial regression with spatial eigenvector filtering and Getis-Ord Gi* hot spot analysis across five pandemic periods aligned with major policy shifts. The analysis revealed a detection paradox. Early hot spots concentrated in lower-income census block groups (median household income: $52,022–$55,676), but by September 2020, hot spots had shifted to more affluent areas (median: $77,069). Historically Black neighborhoods along the I-95 corridor emerged as persistent cold spots despite multiple structural risk factors: lower incomes, reduced insurance coverage, and limited healthcare access. From Period 3 onward, predominantly Black census block groups showed significantly lower reported rates (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 0.991–0.995, p < 0.001). Household overcrowding was tested but retained in no final model. These paradoxical patterns suggest that as testing expanded, surveillance increasingly tracked healthcare utilization rather than transmission. What appeared as neighborhood “protection” likely reflected barriers to testing access shaped by transportation constraints, work schedule inflexibility, and historical relationships with medical institutions. Census block group analysis revealed these dynamics obscured at broader geographic scales. The findings challenge the assumption that reported case rates approximate true disease burden and have direct implications for emergency response planning: surveillance systems require complementary detection streams, risk-adjusted monitoring for underdetection, and targeted outreach where poverty and limited access to testing are concentrated but reported rates are low.
n02a00539f893: Background Viral meningitis remains a significant global public health problem, particularly in resource-limited settings where the diagnosis of viral etiology is mainly based on clinical assessment. This study aimed to identify the common viral etiologies of meningitis, describe their associated clinical features, and assess patient outcomes among individuals suspected of meningitis without evidence of bacterial meningitis. Methods We conducted a multicenter study involving 430 patients clinically suspected of meningitis. Clinical data and cerebrospinal fluid samples (CSF) were collected following standard procedures. Viral nucleic acids were extracted from CSF specimens. Complementary DNA was prepared from viral RNA using reverse transcription. Viral nucleic acids were amplified and detected using qualitative conventional polymerase chain reactions. Patient outcomes were evaluated using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS). Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with unfavorable patient outcomes, with statistical significance set at a p-value < 0.05 at a 95% confidence level. Results The prevalence of viral meningitis was 52.8% (227/430). Enteroviruses were the most common, 47.9% (206/430), followed by herpes simplex virus-1, 2.8% (12/430), herpes simplex virus-2, 1.4% (6/430), and Epstein-Barr virus, 0.7% (3/430). Overall, 6.7% (29/430) of study participants experienced unfavorable outcomes (GOS = 1–4). Factors independently associated with unfavorable outcomes included sex (AOR = 2.684, 95% CI = 1.177–6.119), duration from disease onset to hospital visit (AOR = 1.433, 95% CI = 1.043–1.967), and history of antibiotic intake before hospital visit (AOR = 2.784, 95% CI = 1.270–6.104). Conclusions In this predominantly pediatric study, enteroviruses are the leading cause of viral meningitis in Ethiopia. Most study participants experienced favorable outcomes. Unfavorable outcomes were independently associated with sex, duration from disease onset to hospital visit, and history of antibiotic use before hospital visit. Further identification and characterization of Enteroviruses are warranted.
n7117b4ebcca0: Background The contribution of sagittal spinal alignment to sensorimotor function in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) remains unclear. We examined whether thoracic kyphosis (TK) is associated with sensory integration and postural balance in patients with AIS, independent of coronal structural misalignment. Methods Forty-five AIS patients (Cobb angle ≥ 10°) were consecutively recruited from the outpatient rehabilitation clinic of a university-affiliated hospital (median age 11.0 years, IQR 10.0–13.0; 33 female). There was no selection criterion related to kyphosis. All participants were newly screened and had not yet initiated scoliosis-specific exercise, physiotherapy, or brace treatment. Participants completed the Sensory Organization Test (SOT) and full-spine radiography. Five sensory ratios and four postural control indices were derived from SOT condition-level equilibrium scores (ES). The C4/C1 ratio reflects the ability to maintain postural stability when somatosensory input is disrupted by a sway-referenced support surface (C4) relative to a fixed surface (C1). Associations were examined with Spearman and partial Spearman correlations (adjusting for Cobb angle, age, and BMI) and tertile comparisons with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Findings Forty-two patients had complete data for primary analyses (median Cobb angle 15.3°, IQR 11.2°–20.0°). Greater TK was associated with a higher C4/C1 ratio (Spearman ρ = 0.416, p = 0.006), and this association remained significant after adjustment for Cobb angle, age, and BMI (partial Spearman ρ = 0.475, p = 0.002). Cobb angle was not associated with any sensory ratio (all p > 0.1) but was positively associated with firm-surface equilibrium scores (C1: ρ = 0.525, p < 0.001). The C4/C1 ratio increased monotonically across TK tertiles (Low 0.701 → Mid 0.832 → High 0.861; Kruskal-Wallis H = 8.58, p = 0.014) and was associated with better postural control across all domains (composite ES: ρ = 0.453; variability: ρ = −0.410; adaptation: ρ = 0.433; all p < 0.01). Interpretation TK and Cobb angle showed differential associations with postural control: TK was associated with the C4/C1 ratio, whereas Cobb angle was associated with firm-surface stability. The C4/C1 ratio statistically carried the association between TK and postural control via an indirect-only pathway. These findings suggest that sagittal and coronal spinal parameters are differentially associated with postural control, which may inform future research on phenotype-specific assessment strategies.
n1244691a4e1e: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21REINS) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21REINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.
nd029882b919f: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.
nf4f0b11fa06c: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral–caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.
na3412ebfff91: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.
nae30eedf1261: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.
n0ab99943e7ed: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. Here, we identify factors suppressing Th17 responses during primary infection. We demonstrate that the lack of Th17 induction is independent of route and duration. Next, using Tbx21-deficient mice, we show that Mtb drives a Th1 response that is only partially protective and limits Th17 cell production in an IFN-γ-independent manner. We further reveal that the ESX-1 type VII secretion system and lipid phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) suppress Th17 responses. Infection with ESX-1 or PDIM mutants results in significantly increased Th17 T cells and IL-17A cytokine in the lungs, and infection of IL-17A-deficient animals partially restores virulence of ESX-1 and PDIM mutants. Although the ESX-1 secretion system and lipid PDIM elicit type I IFN, which can suppress Th17 differentiation, we find that suppression of Th17 is independent of type I IFN. Instead, ESX-1 and PDIM suppress production of IL-23, a cytokine that promotes Th17 differentiation, in dendritic cells found in mediastinal lymph nodes during Mtb infection. These findings define a new function of the ESX-1 secretion system and PDIM in Mtb virulence, a long-standing question in tuberculosis research.
n089630dc6e4b: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women’s health.
n982e6e4d7d55: In this autobiography, I describe my childhood and early education and summarize structural biology research in nucleic acids and proteins and my work with the Protein Data Bank.
ncea4acd33b2d: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.
n7f3c4ea9b936: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 (“Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals”). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.
n969eeae3fe7d: by Hugo G. Castelán-Sánchez, Art F. Y. Poon Recombination is an important process in the evolution of RNA viruses. For viruses with segmented genomes, recombination can occur by reassortment of entire genomic segments. This process has played a significant role in the adaptation and spread of influenza viruses with novel genomic combinations, i.e., antigenic shifts. Reassortment is usually identified by discrepancies between the topologies of trees reconstructed from different genomic segments, e.g., subtree prune and regraft (SPR) rearrangements. However, this phylogenetic discordance can also result from errors in tree reconstruction due to insufficient information. The objective of this study was to evaluate the contribution of phylogenetic reconstruction error to the inference of reassortment events from influenza A virus (IAV) genomes from avian hosts. We curated a dataset of 11,795 complete avian H5Nx IAV genomes and sampled subsets of HA sequences with different expected levels of reconstruction error. Next, we simulated molecular evolution along the trees reconstructed from these HA samples, varying rates of evolution and sequence lengths to correspond to the other genomic segments. Because these simulations had no reassortment, any phylogenetic discordance identified from the resulting trees must be caused by reconstruction error. We found that simulations from random samples yielded about 32% as many SPRs as obtained from real data. This false positive rate was reduced to 4% when simulating trees from the most genetically divergent subset of HA sequences. By modifying the simulated trees with SPR rearrangements, we observed a false negative rate of 8.5%, which increased with the number of SPRs per tree. Overall, we found that reassortment can be substantially overestimated from phylogenetic discordance, underscoring the need to account for phylogenetic uncertainty and sampling design when analyzing IAV datasets for reassortment.
n9957dc7e8ac0: Background Postoperative delirium (POD) is a fluctuating confusional state occurring early after surgery. Given its fluctuating nature, POD detection is influenced by the frequency and timing of screening. Sparse assessments potentially underestimate the true incidence reported in individual studies, subsequently influencing the weight of studies in meta-analyses, and the results and precision of these meta-analyses. Objective To develop a method to evaluate the robustness of meta-analyses to the variation in the frequency and timing of POD assessment across included studies. Methods We developed an expert-based scoring system to rate studies according to the confidence that a patient reported not to have POD in the study truly did not, based on the reported timing and frequency of POD assessments. We describe how to use the system to generate hypothetical event rates for studies if the frequency and timing of POD assessment were optimal and how to use these rates in a sensitivity analysis of meta-analyses including these studies. We illustrate the method applying it to two meta-analyses as work examples, one of observational studies and one of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Results In our work examples, the expert-based score for the individual studies ranged from 33–77% for the observational and 22–70% for RCTs meta-analysis. Sensitivity analyses showed a change in the pooled effect size, heterogeneity, and precision compared to the original estimates. Conclusion We present a method to evaluate the robustness of a meta-analysis of studies having POD as an outcome, when there is variation across individual studies in the frequency and timing of POD assessment. The confidence score acts as a preliminary index of the robustness of meta-analyses. Through work examples, we showed that the robustness depends on the characteristics of individual studies included.
n67c22a2c10d1: Background Diabetic Neuropathy (DN) is a prevalent complication of diabetes linked to chronic inflammation. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Interleukin-10 (IL-10) are key cytokines implicated in DN pathogenesis. This study investigates the association of IL6 and IL10 gene polymorphisms and serum levels with DN in the Bangladeshi population. Materials and methods A case-control study was conducted with 225 participants: diabetic patients with DN (n = 75), diabetic patients without DN (n = 75), and healthy controls (n = 75). Genomic DNA was extracted for genotyping IL-6 (rs1800796) and IL-10 (rs1800896) SNPs via PCR. Serum cytokine levels were measured using ELISA. Results Serum IL-6 levels were significantly higher in the DN group than in the other study groups (p < 0.0001), with the highest levels observed among individuals with the IL-6 rs1800796 CC genotype. In unadjusted analyses, the IL-6 CC genotype was associated with increased odds of DN compared with healthy controls (OR = 4.813, 95% CI: 1.752–13.85, p = 0.0040), as was the IL-10 GG genotype (OR = 2.679, 95% CI: 1.000–6.751, p = 0.0373). However, neither IL-6 nor IL-10 genotype remained independently associated with DN after multivariable adjustment. Serum IL-10 levels did not differ significantly among the study groups (p = 0.0948). Combined genotype analyses showed several nominal associations, although these findings were exploratory. Serum IL-6 showed promising discriminatory ability in distinguishing patients with DN from the other study groups, whereas IL-10 demonstrated limited discriminatory performance. Conclusion These findings support further investigation of serum IL-6 as a potential candidate biomarker for diabetic neuropathy, whereas the independent contribution of the investigated IL-6 and IL-10 polymorphisms remains uncertain. Larger prospective studies with independent external validation are required before clinical application can be considered.
n182af9794a4b: This study examines whether consumers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for ready-to-eat cereals differs between immersive virtual reality (IVR) and real-world (RW) environments. Real choice experiments were conducted with 227 respondents who selected reservation dates without knowing whether they corresponded to the IVR or RW setting. To derive consumers’ WTP, random parameter logit models were estimated primarily in WTP space, while preference-space models were used as a robustness check. The results show no significant differences in WTP between IVR and RW for any of the cereal products tested. This suggests that consumers’ product choices in IVR environments are based on monetary valuations, similar to those in real environments. When combined with real economic incentives, IVR-based choice experiments may therefore yield WTP estimates comparable to those obtained from conventional real choice experiments. To our knowledge, this is the first study to compare WTP between IVR and RW environments using an incentive-compatible experimental design.
n8a42ae64954c: Quantum neural networks learn by following gradients, and on real hardware those gradients are washed out by noise. Predicting how quickly this happens, before any finite noise experiment or circuit sweep is run, remains an open problem. We present CohAlign, an open source toolkit that computes the first order noise susceptibility of the ensemble second moment of a specified parameter gradient in a charge conserving brickwork quantum neural network. The computation needs only a classical description of the circuit, the noise model, the prepared state, the readout and the initialisation prior. The predicted quantity is distinct from training convergence or final accuracy. The key observation is that only the part of the noise that a measurement can actually see matters. A purposefully constructed control channel makes this clear, damaging the operator carrying a gradient at nearly the maximal rate while the measured gradient remains exactly as predicted and untouched. We validate the predictions against separately evaluated finite difference slopes across the benchmark suite, including a signed coherent case, in exact simulations at eight and ten qubits and on two circuit topologies.
n972dce73c098: Introduction Postoperative pain after cesarean section may delay recovery and impair function. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and low-level laser photobiomodulation (PBM) are used for pain control, but the additional effect of combining these therapies remains unclear. This study investigated this effect. Methods A randomized clinical trial with four groups: combined TENS + low-level laser photobiomodulation (PBM), TENS alone, placebo, and control. Assessments were performed at 8–12 h (t1), 20–24 h (t2), and 44–48 h postpartum (t3). Outcomes included pain intensity, functional independence, functional capacity assessed by the Two-Minute Walk Test (2MWT), and cardiorespiratory variables. Two intervention sessions were applied after t1 and t2, except in the control group. Data were analyzed using mixed ANOVA and nonparametric equivalents when appropriate. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 88 women were included. Pain intensity decreased significantly over time in the combined TENS + PBM group (1.82 ± 1.18 at t2 vs 1.30 ± 0.86 at t3; p = 0.008) and in the TENS group (1.59 ± 1.05 at t2 vs 0.95 ± 1.05 at t3; p = 0.025). Functional independence increased in the combined therapy group (14.9 ± 3.3 at t1 vs 17.1 ± 3.6 at t3; p = 0.034) and in the TENS group (15.2 ± 3.0 at t1 vs 17.5 ± 3.4 at t3; p = 0.028). Functional capacity improved in all groups between t2 and t3 in the Two-Minute Walk Test (Control: 63.5 vs 76.8 m, p = 0.002; Placebo: 50.3 vs 63.9 m, p = 0.002; Combined: 48.3 vs 65.2 m, p = 0.0006; TENS: 61.1 vs 72.2 m, p = 0.005). No significant differences were observed between groups (p > 0.05). A significant time effect was found for pain (p < 0.05) and functional independence (p < 0.001). Conclusion Pain decreased and functional independence improved during the postoperative period. However, the combination of TENS and low-level laser photobiomodulation did not provide additional benefits compared with the other groups.
n378f05f25205: Deep-learning-based holographic reconstruction requires numerical data with reliable ground truth for training and quantitative evaluation. Experimental hologram acquisition and pixel-level phase annotation can be difficult to control, making physically defined numerical cases useful as reproducible benchmarks. Here, three analytically specified phase targets—a smooth Gaussian distribution, a four-level step distribution, and a radially structured Siemens Star—are used to generate off-axis digital holograms with known phase ground truth. A frequency-domain filtering procedure is applied before inverse Fourier reconstruction, followed by DCT-based global phase unwrapping. Reconstruction quality is quantified using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), correlation coefficient, and profile-based error analysis. The results show that reconstruction errors are comparatively small in smooth regions and increase near abrupt or high-spatial-frequency phase transitions. The three cases are therefore presented as controlled benchmark examples for algorithm verification and baseline comparison, not as a complete substitute for experimental holographic datasets or as a complete training corpus for deep-learning models.
n0a03e162c363: by Melissa A. Hausburg, Kaysie L. Banton, Christopher D. Cassidy, Robert M. Madayag, Carlos H. Palacio, Jason S. Williams, Gregory W. Thomas, Raphael Bar-Or, David Bar-Or Systemic inflammatory response syndrome, driven by trauma or infection, involves excessive innate immune activation. Dexamethasone (DEX), a synthetic glucocorticoid, suppresses inflammation, although adverse side effects limit its clinical use. The inflammasome, a multiprotein complex that assembles in response to inflammatory stimuli like ATP after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) priming, facilitates caspase-1 cleavage and release of the proinflammatory cytokine, interleukin (IL)-1β. We investigated whether DEX and decanoic acid (DA), a saturated medium-chain fatty acid, inhibited caspase-1 activity and IL-1β release in an LPS/ATP-stimulated THP-1 macrophage model and whether co-treatment would allow for pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing in vitro. PMA-differentiated THP-1macrophages were primed with LPS overnight and stimulated with ATP for 3 h in the presence of DA, DEX, or both. Viability and cytotoxicity were assessed. Caspase-1 activity and IL-1β were quantified, and EC50 values were calculated by nonlinear regression. In control conditions, LPS/ATP stimulation induced 5.56 (q1: 3.51 – q3: 6.38) ng/mL of IL-1β release. DA and DEX inhibited IL-1β with full dose-response EC50 values of 131.7 μM and 24.29 nM, respectively. DA concentrations exceeding 800 μM decreased cell viability. An 8 x 9-point DA/DEX dose matrix (0–500 μM DA; 0 to 1e4 nM DEX) was used to interrogate drug interaction for IL-1β inhibition and caspase-1 activity. DEX EC50 values remained within a narrow 95% confidence interval of 17.5–26.6 nM, regardless of DA background concentration. DA reduced caspase-1 enzymatic activity with a calculated EC50 value of ~140 μM; whereas, DEX did not. These data show that DA and DEX act independently. Furthermore, compared to DEX alone, the presence of DA allowed for equivalent in vitro IL-1β suppression at lower DEX concentrations, supporting pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing. Determination of whether this pharmacologic effect translates to clinically meaningful corticosteroid dose reduction requires further study.
n75be20aa55f8: Surface electromyography (sEMG) has emerged as an impactful tool for controlling advanced prosthetic devices by detecting and recording muscle electrical activity during motion. This study presents a unique technique for recognizing nine distinct classes of finger movements by utilizing the Ninapro database.
